source_text.body:
Underwrite a multifamily deal in minutes
An investor used Claude Cowork to underwrite a 47-unit value-add deal, researching crime, rents and vacancy and flagging a utility-cost recovery opportunity.
Done with
CW
Claude Cowork
CC
Claude Code
What they did
Carl Mcknight downloaded the offering memorandum, T12 and rent roll for a 47-unit Kentucky property and uploaded them to the agent. It reviewed them, researched crime, rents, comps and vacancy, normalized expenses, and modeled upside, financing and offer tiers. It also questioned the utility-billing (RUBS) assumption on its own.
How it went
Normalized NOI came out at $147,055 against the seller's $161,691, mainly because management fees were missing. He modeled a $1,475,000 target price and a conservative stabilized NOI of $221,857 without RUBS. Plumbing and studio vacancy stayed open questions.
Worth knowing
The agent's market rents probably already include utilities, so he left RUBS out of his base case. Also verify the plumbing and management-fee gaps before trusting the numbers.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Cowork
Copy prompt
I'm considering buying a [number]-unit [property type] at [address or city] for [asking price]. Research local crime trends, market rents, and vacancy for [neighborhood], then build a simple underwriting spreadsheet from the rent roll and expenses I've attached. Flag any upside such as utility-cost recovery or below-market rents, and finish with a one-page summary showing your assumptions, estimated returns, and the biggest risks.
Original source: https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/80/topics/1281269-using-claude-cowork-to-underwrite-a-deal-in-10-mins
